Subject: URGENT: HealthSync hosted API latency spike impacting nightly ingest

Camila —

We're seeing a major degradation on the Redwood hosted API starting ~07:45 PST this morning during our nightly clinical ingest. Key metrics: p95 generation latency jumped from ~180ms to ~2.4s; p99 spiked to ~6.8s and we observed increased 5xx errors ~3.2% during the window. This is affecting patient ingest and downstream validation jobs (batch IDs: bs-1189, bs-1190).

We pushed a large batch with extended context (most requests ~14k–18k tokens) to test new clinical summarization prompts; latency was fine in lower load earlier this week. Attached is our p95 export for the last 4 hours.

Request: can Redwood triage now and either (a) apply an immediate mitigation to reduce tail latency or (b) advise a temporary throttle limit we should apply on our side? This is high-severity for our ops team.

Thanks,

On Thu, Nov 1, 2028 at 08:25 AM camila_reyes <camila@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Forwarding HealthSync escalation — they just sent the p95 export. Impact: p95/p99 regression aligned with a burst of 14k–18k context requests.

Triage notes (initial):
- Observed queue backlog on request-shard q-17 beginning 07:40 PST; queue depth rose ~7x.
- Backend traces show a sharp increase in decode time for the quantized model variant redwood-32k-q4 at sequence lengths > 12k. CPU/GPU utilization looks normal on the host, but the per-request decode time dominates.
- KV cache miss rate for HealthSync tenant jumped from 12% -> 46% (their prompt mixes many unique patient histories). Cache warming ineffective for burst pattern.
- Error spike corresponds to transient timeouts at our load-balancer when queueing > 2s.

Immediate mitigation applied (09:00 PST):
- Enabled per-tenant soft throttle: max_concurrency=4, max_inflight_tokens=16000 for tenant HS-3472 (HealthSync).
- Engaged forced fallback to redwood-lite-8k-q4 for requests with >16k tokens (we now block and return clear 429-style advisory to customer SDK for >24k).
- Warmed cache for frequent prefixes used in their production jobs.

Preliminary impact: within 18 minutes p95 decreased from 2.4s to ~360ms for mixed traffic; p99 trending down but still elevated (~1.1s). Will continue to monitor.

Attachments: heap_profile_20281101.txt (attached), Grafana snapshot: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/hosted/healthsync-p95-20281101

Next steps I suggest:
1) Short window config rollout to keep fallback for 4 hours and observe.
2) Product/Model to evaluate long-context kernel performance for redwood-32k-q4 variant — likely decoder path regression at these sequence lengths.
3) Discuss longer term: prefix/KV caching improvements and per-tenant cold-start protections.

- Aditya (on-call SRE)

Aisha / Tom —

Thanks again for the quick heads-up this morning and for the export — that was very helpful. Summary of what we did and next steps: 

What happened (summary)
- Starting ~07:40 PST a burst of requests with extended context (~14k–18k tokens) from a HealthSync job caused queueing and increased decode time for our redwood-32k-q4 variant, which created elevated p95/p99 and transient 5xx timeouts.

Immediate mitigations applied (completed by 09:05 PST)
- Soft per-tenant throttles applied: max_concurrency=4 and max_inflight_tokens=16000
- Requests with >16k tokens were routed to a fallback variant (redwood-lite-8k-q4) where appropriate; we now return clear SDK advisory/errors for requests exceeding hard limits to avoid silent timeouts
- Cache warms for common prefixes and additional monitoring to detect recurrence

Observed impact
- p95 improved from ~2.4s to ~260–360ms within 30 minutes of mitigations; p99 reduced but is still stabilizing (~950ms at last check).

Next steps (our plan)
- We will keep the fallback and throttles in place for a 6 hour observation window and monitor closely.
- Product & Research will run a perf investigation into redwood-32k-q4 decoder behavior for contexts >12k and propose a patch or alternate variant (we will share a timeline within 48 hours).
- We will follow up with a formal incident summary and a proposed credit for the impacted window (Laura has approved up to 30% as an upper bound; we'll quantify precisely).

We've opened INC-8421 for tracking and attached the p95 export and heap profile we collected. Relevant tracker: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-8421. HubSpot case: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/HS-3472

Please let me know if you want a bridge — I can set one up. Apologies for the disruption and thank you for your patience as we stabilize.

—Camila Reyes
